origin: it should NOT report an issue if t() is used in a spec
source:
defmodule CorrectUsage do
  @spec f(MyApp.MyStruct.t()) :: any
  def f(_) do
    "yay"
  end

  @spec g(any, AStruct.t()) :: MyApp.MyStruct.t()
  def g(_, _) do
    "yay"
  end
end

origin: it should NOT report an issue for functions, macros, or variables named spec
source:
defmodule IgnoredFunction do
  def spec(%AStruct{}) do
    "okay"
  end

  def spec(arg) when arg == %AStruct{} do
    arg
  end
end

origin: it should report an issue if a struct is used as a parameter in a spec
source:
defmodule Offender do
  @spec f(any, %MyApp.MyStruct{}, any) :: any
  def f(_, _, _) do
    "oops"
  end
end

origin: it should report an issue if a struct is used as a return value in a spec
it should report an issue if a struct is part of a union in a spec
source:
defmodule Offender do
  alias MyApp.MyStruct, as: MS
  @spec f(String.t() | %MS{} | integer) :: any
  def f(_) do
    "oops"
  end
end

origin: it should report an issue if a struct is used as an argument in a spec
source:
defmodule Offender do
  alias MyApp.MyStruct
  @spec f(arg) :: any when arg: %MyStruct{}
  def f(_) do
    "oops"
  end
end

origin: it should report an issue if a struct has an argument name in a spec
source:
defmodule Offender do
  @spec f(my_struct :: %MyApp.MyStruct{}) :: any
  def f(_) do
    "oops"
  end
end

origin: it should report multiple issues in separate specs
source:
defmodule Offender do
  @spec f(my_struct :: %MyApp.MyStruct{}) :: any
  def f(_) do
    "oops"
  end

  @spec g(a_struct :: %AStruct{}) :: any
  def g(_) do
    "oops"
  end
end

origin: it should report multiple issues in a single spec
source:
defmodule Offender do
  @spec f(a_struct :: %AStruct{}, my_struct :: %MyApp.MyStruct{}) :: any
  def f(_, _) do
    "oops"
  end
end
